title: ASP.NET Core Configuration with Azure
description: Wire Azure App Configuration, Key Vault, and managed identity into ASP.NET Core configuration.

data.text: In production, ASP.NET Core apps often need feature flags, environment-specific settings, and centralized configuration. Azure App Configuration provides a hosted key-value store that integrates with Key Vault and feature management.

data.title: Register Azure App Configuration with Key Vault references
data.content: Load configuration from Azure App Configuration and resolve Key Vault references automatically.

data.text: Feature flags let you turn features on or off without redeploying. The `Microsoft.FeatureManagement` package integrates with Azure App Configuration.

data.title: Feature flag example
data.content: Define a feature flag in Azure App Configuration and read it in middleware or controllers.

data.title: Refresh configuration
data.text: Azure App Configuration can push configuration changes to your app using the `RefreshOn` option or by calling `app.Configuration.Refresh()` from an endpoint.

data.title: Add App Configuration to an existing app
data.description: Move application settings from appsettings.json into Azure App Configuration.
steps: Create an Azure App Configuration store in the Azure portal
Import settings from appsettings.json into App Configuration
Wire App Configuration into Program.cs using the code above
Add a feature flag and test it in the running app
data.expectedOutcome: The app reads configuration values from Azure App Configuration and respects the feature flag.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure App Configuration centralizes settings across environments
Feature flags support gradual rollouts and instant rollbacks
App Configuration integrates with Key Vault for secret references
Use `DefaultAzureCredential` for zero-secret local and cloud authentication
data.takeaway: Combining App Configuration, Key Vault, and managed identity gives you a complete, production-ready configuration story for ASP.NET Core.
